_comment: Findings that are already public and cannot be unpublished.
These are versions of SECURITY.md, in commits that shipped before 2026-08-13, which
named the maintainer account's plan and queried organisation-scoped API fields. HEAD is
clean; the working-tree scan that CI runs on every push reports zero. What remains is
history, and rewriting history would NOT remove it: the old blobs stay reachable by
commit SHA until GitHub garbage-collects them, which only support can trigger. So the
decision on record is to leave the history intact and to state plainly what it contains.
This file is an ALLOW-list of accepted, already-published findings, not a way to silence
the check. scripts/check_disclosure.py --history --baseline <this file> fails on anything
NOT listed here, and reports any entry here that no longer matches as a stale exemption.
Adding a line is a deliberate act: it says 'this is public, we know, and we accept it'.
accepted: 21c757b:SECURITY.md

forbidden pattern (?i)\b(?:this|our)\s+(?:org|organisation|organization|account)\s+is\s+on\s+the\b — Names the tier or plan this account holds. Say that a paid tier is required and link the vendor's documentation; which tier is held adds nothing a reader can act on.
21c757b:SECURITY.md
forbidden pattern \.plan\.name — GET /orgs/{org} returns the billing plan only to members. Publishing it discloses account information no reader of this repository needs.
21c757b:SECURITY.md
forbidden pattern advanced_security_enabled — An organisation-wide security posture field. State this repository's own security_and_analysis instead.
21c757b:SECURITY.md

forbidden pattern gh api orgs/ — An organisation-scoped API call reads account state that is wider than this repository and, for some fields, is visible only to members. Scope verification commands to the repository.
